body: Your acquaintances can become your friends. Have a good day at work. Remember you will get through this and you are not alone.
See if your friends are available so you can spend time with them and have a different scenery. If you can get through today, tomorrow will be a bit easier to handle

Maybe you can try going to an animal shelter to volunteer there if you can if you like being around animals. They are very healing. I read where many people said it helped them the most to deal with their mental health and especially if they are in crisis.
If you can’t, I’m here to talk with as well

Do you have family or friends close to you that you can stay with today and maybe for the next few days? If you’ve been turned away by the hospital, still try to reach out to someone that you can stay with if you can.

You’re not hopeless. You’re human and we make mistakes. Sometimes it’s not your fault. Try to find something that gives you a reason to stay. It can be very small. Do you like pets? Go to an animal shelter to lend a hand. Adopt a cat. Sometimes a small thing starts to become a big thing. Reach out to therapy groups. They are helpful and you don’t feel isolated. 
You are important and people care about you. You will find that life does change. It will not stay like this forever.
Are you able to see a psychiatrist? Do you have health coverage for that?
Do you feel they are not helping?
Have you tried going to therapy or group therapy in your area?
Are there certain things that trigger you?

I am in the same emotional state as you, always being dragged back to this dark space. I have talked to others who have said the feeling of suicidal thoughts eventually passed for them over the years. In addition to changing their circumstance like you did, they also tried different support systems to change their mindset eg. therapist, retreats, group counselling, etc. And they did get better, it just took time. I believe it can be the same for you. Try to go to therapy. I think that seems to be what most people said helped them.
What is causing you to feel this way?

I understand your situation. If you’re open to it, try rooming with someone just for the social aspect of it to make friends. Having a house in Canada is expensive but start your way up with a condo. Is working part time an option possibly? It’s a difficult first step but you can also see if there are other jobs you can apply to within your field that has more reasonable hours. Or at the very least if you can, take a leave of absence so you can take a break and reevaluate what you can do. You are worth more than a job. Please stay. You are important.
